chapter_theme: A song at Thiruppazhuvur (திருப்பழுவூர்): a catalogue of prostitutes with foul mouths, love-drugs in rice and dancing seductions, and the question whether kinship with them can be; the praise tells Krishna's part in the Bharata war.

890.reading: The poet lists the price-women who speak crooked troubling words, whose mouths stink, who size up men, kindle their desire, and serve rice mixed with a drug, who bathe in unguents, dance with anklets, and whirl men with seductive eyes and swaying waists, and asks whether kinship with such prostitutes can be. The praise names Krishna, who darkened the sun with his discus and finished the Bharata war, killing brothers, uncles, elders and sons of the Kauravas until foxes and ghouls fed on the field, praised by the devotees and the Pandavas, as uncle, and Murugan with his peacock that shakes mountain and sea, at Pazhuvur.
890.nuance: இடும் மருந்தொடு சோற்றையே இடு விலைமாதர்: the women feed men rice laced with a drug, a charge of love-medicine (வசிய மருந்து) beyond the usual deceit. திகிரி கொண்டு இருளாக்கி: Krishna hiding the sun with his discus, from the Mahabharata war. The Pandava lines (அரி அருளும் மைந்தர்கள்) are my reading.
